items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: It was a lady teacher. I never will forget her, her name, Margaret Reed, and we had a beautiful time there.

ctx.x: It was a lady teacher. I never will forget her, her name, Margaret Reed, and we had a beautiful time there. It didn't make any difference to her whether I could read or not, you know. We happened to have -- when I changed over to the bass fiddle, I used to play a little violin too in the orchestra, but I changed over real quick.

They had a, happened to have a bass fiddle in the orchestra rooms, which I became very interested in, and I asked her, could I use it, you know, could I try it out. And she said, go ahead. And like I say, right there one of the fiddle players showed me how to tune, because it's the reverse from the little violin.
